text: True or False: The well-ordering principle for ℕ states that every non-empty subset of ℕ has a greatest element.
explanation: False. The well-ordering principle says every non-empty subset of ℕ has a least (smallest) element, not a greatest one — indeed ℕ itself has no greatest element. This least-element property underlies minimal-counterexample proofs and is equivalent to induction.
